description: The Environment Agency's real-time flood monitoring API gives open, near real-time access to flood warnings and flood alerts, the flood areas they apply to, water level and flow measurements, rainfall and tide gauge readings, and metadata on the monitoring stations across England. Levels and flows are usually measured every 15 minutes, though stations report back once or twice a day in quiet periods and more often when flood risk rises. It is a REST service returning JSON, with CSV for some lists, filters by river, catchment, town, parameter or distance, and a single call for the latest value of every measure; readings are also archived daily as CSV dump files in short and full formats. The data are free under the Open Government Licence with no registration, and users are asked to credit the Environment Agency real-time data API. Caveats: the service is labelled beta, offers no guaranteed service level and must not be used for safety-critical applications, readings sometimes arrive in late batches so the latest-value call alone does not keep a complete history, and coverage is England only. Simulation uses: live inputs for flood forecasting and digital twins, event reconstruction of river and coastal floods for drainage, dam and defence studies, trigger thresholds for emergency response, and calibration of hydraulic models. Related records: the UK National River Flow Archive (data-uk-national-river-flow-archive) and EA flood defence assets (data-ea-aims-spatial-flood-defences).
